style_when: the story is about change after hours — automation displacing shifts, a market open all night, capacity running while people sleep
prompt: An architectural photograph of a towering automated warehouse aisle with robotic shuttle storage at blue hour. 35mm anamorphic wide, extreme asymmetry with heavy editorial framing, the massive steel storage grid commands the right side. Deep blue ambient light fills the dark warehouse aisle, contrasting with warm amber status lights on the moving robotic shuttles. Clean geometry, deep industrial contrast, galvanized steel and graphite materials. No moving figures, long-exposure calm, no text, no logos.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, UI elements, people
rationale: The article is about the systemic shift in how warehouse automation capacity is sold and measured, often operating around the clock under robotics-as-a-service models. Architectural night captures this automated capacity running without human labor, emphasizing the scale of the investment and the twilight opacity of the vendor's financial models.
subject: an automated warehouse storage aisle with robotic shuttles at twilight
core_thesis: The inputs to a warehouse automation business case now come from the vendor selling the system, so operators can only defend the loaded cost per unit of work and peak volume share.
core_conflict: Vendor-supplied payback models vs operator-measured cost per unit of work.
composition: extreme asymmetry with heavy editorial framing
